I’ll describe it like a “product sheet” for your buildathon demo.

🏷 Name & Tagline

App name: RiderMate
Tagline: “Your AI-powered ride safety and coaching companion for two-wheeler riders.”

📱 Platforms

Android APK

Built via GitHub Actions (flutter build apk --release)

Installable on phone as app-release.apk

Web (browser)

Runs via flutter run -d web-server or -d chrome in Codespaces

Great for testing + demo on laptop

🧱 Main Screens & What Actually Works
1️⃣ Login / Profile (Basic)

What you have:

Simple profile setup (name, age, city, vehicle type, weight) stored locally.

Can be used by AI Coach to personalize advice (“for a rider in Bangalore…”).

What is not in v1:

No real Google Sign-In yet (no Firebase Auth).

No multi-user accounts / backend user database.

For buildathon, this is okay — judges care more about the ride + AI experience than auth.

2️⃣ Home Screen

What you see:

A clean dashboard with cards / buttons to:

Start Ride

Open AI Coach

View Ride History

Open Memories

See Friends / Travel with friends

Access Leaderboard / Referrals

What it does:

Just a simple, modern navigation hub into all major features.

No heavy logic here — but it makes the app feel like a real product, not a demo.

3️⃣ Live Ride Tracking (Core Feature)

What works:

Start / Stop Ride button:

Starts a ride session.

Ends ride, saves it to RideHistoryService.

Uses geolocator for:

GPS permission

Location stream

Current speed (km/h)

You can show:

Current speed

Distance travelled

Elapsed time

Overspeed detection:

If speed > defined limit (e.g., 60 km/h or configurable):

Set a flag like isOverspeeding.

Show a red warning banner: “Slow down! You’re over the safe limit.”

Count overspeed events for that ride.

Points system per ride:

Example:

10 points per km

Bonus for safe ride (no overspeed)

Points stored in the ride data.

Ride saved to history:

On stop, a Ride object is created:

distanceKm

startTime, endTime

overspeedEvents

pointsEarned

Stored in RideHistoryService.rides.

What is partial:

Real-time map path (polyline on Google Map) is not yet fully wired.

Background tracking (screen off) is not implemented — demo focuses on foreground tracking.

For buildathon, foreground live tracking + stats + overspeed warning is strong enough.

4️⃣ Ride History

What works:

List of all saved rides from RideHistoryService.

For each ride, you display:

Distance (km)

Duration (minutes)

Points

Overspeed count

On tapping a ride:

Optional detail view showing per-ride stats:

Distance

Duration

Start/End time

Overspeed events

Safety comment (e.g., “Safe / Improve / Risky” based on overspeeds)

This gives judges a sense of progress and data collection over time.

5️⃣ AI Ride Coach (Buildathon Hero Feature)

Backed by your Gemini backend, this is the star.

Data used:

From all rides in last 7 days:

totalKmWeek

totalRidesWeek

totalOverspeedsWeek

totalPointsWeek

For last ride:

Distance

Minutes

Average speed

Overspeed events

Safety score (0–100) computed from overspeed events.

🧾 a) Weekly Summary + Safety Score

On opening the AI Coach tab, the app:

Calls AICoachService.computeStats() to create a CoachStats object.

Sends stats to your Gemini backend via /ai-coach.

Backend builds a prompt that says:

You are RiderMate, an AI coach in India

Here are the rider’s stats

Give summary + practical tips

Gemini returns text like:

“This week you rode 45 km over 3 rides. Your safety score is 82/100. Overall safe, but you had 4 overspeed events. Try to slow down near junctions and avoid sudden speed bursts…”

In UI you show:

Text block: “AI summary & recommendations”

Colored safety score:

Green if high

Orange if medium

Red if low

❓ b) Ask AI Coach Anything (Chat)

What works:

User types a question in a text field:

“How can I ride safely at night?”

“How often should I rest on a 200 km trip?”

“What food should I eat while riding to avoid sleep?”

On press Send:

Adds a chat bubble (sender: user).

Calls AICoachService.askCoach(stats: _stats, userQuestion: text).

Backend sends stats + question to Gemini.

Gemini returns tailored advice.

App adds AI bubble (sender: ai).

UI behaviour:

Scrollable list of ChatMessages.

Different style for user vs AI bubbles.

Loading spinner while waiting for AI.

This shows real AI integration + context-awareness, perfect for OpenAI × NxtWave judges (even though we’re using Gemini – that’s still valid AI use).

6️⃣ Memories (Location + Notes + Privacy)

What works:

During or after a ride, user can add a Memory:

Note text (like “Nice view spot”)

Current GPS coordinates (lat/lon)

Timestamp

Privacy flag: Public / Friends / Private

Stored in a simple Memory model and local service.

Memories tab shows:

List of memories

Note

Time

Location summary

Privacy tag

What’s partial:

Photo capture:

UI can have “Add photo” icon.

Full wiring to camera + storage is a future extension.

Map view (pins for memories) → not fully done, but list works.

For buildathon, you can say:

“We support ride memories with notes + location + privacy setting. Photo capture and map clustering are planned for the next version.”

7️⃣ Travel with Friends

What you get NOW:

A “Travel with Friends” tab/screen showing:

UI for:

Friend list

Live status (“Riding / Offline”)

“Share ride link” button (UI only)

For buildathon, this is positioned as:

Phase 2 feature – the design and flow are ready.

Real-time multi-user location would require:

Realtime backend (e.g., Firebase or WebSockets)

Authentication

Device tokens

You can still demo it by explaining:

“We’ve designed the travel-with-friends experience and will plug in Firebase/real-time DB next. Our main focus for this buildathon was safety + AI coaching.”

8️⃣ Leaderboard & Referral

What works now (demo-level):

Leaderboard screen:

Shows sample rankings using local data:

You

A few dummy friends

Referral screen:

Shows your “referral code” or invite message.

Copy-to-clipboard style (or just text to share manually).

What’s not in v1:

No real backend tracking of referrals.

No persistent online leaderboard.

But visually, it shows that RiderMate is gamified and has growth mechanisms.

9️⃣ Branding & Build

Custom RiderMate app icon:

assets/logo/icon.png

Generated with flutter_launcher_icons

Dark, modern UI:

Cards, icons, highlight colors (orange / teal).

APK build via GitHub Actions:

Workflow:

Install Flutter

flutter pub get

flutter pub run flutter_launcher_icons

flutter build apk --release

Upload app-release.apk as artifact.

You can download that APK from the GitHub Actions run and install it on your device.

🧠 Tech Stack Summary (for judges)

Frontend: Flutter (Dart)

AI Backend: Node.js (Express) + Google Gemini (gemini-1.5-flash)

Device capabilities:

GPS via geolocator

Local storage (in-memory now; could be Hive/SQLite next)

DevOps:

GitHub Codespaces for cloud dev

GitHub Actions for build pipeline and APK generation

⚠️ Honest Limitations (You Can Mention in Q&A)

AI Coach requires:

Internet connection

Valid Gemini API key in backend

Friends & Leaderboard are designed, but not yet backed by realtime backend.

Ride tracking is foreground-focused; no background service.

Memories photos may be stubbed / limited depending on camera integration status.

But for a student buildathon, what you do have is actually very strong:

Live tracking + Overspeed alerts + History + AI Safety Coach (with real LLM) + Memories + Social & gamification scaffolding + CI/CD + branding.
